subject: Sarcoidosis
object: a rare condition in which small patches of swollen tissue, called granulomas, develop in the organs of the body.
source_quote: Sarcoidosis is a rare condition that causes small patches of swollen tissue, called granulomas, to develop in the organs of the body.

subject: Sarcoidosis
object: no known exact cause.
source_quote: The exact cause of sarcoidosis is not known.

subject: Possible causes of sarcoidosis
object: exposure to substances in the environment (such as mould, wood stoves, soil, tree pollen, insecticides, silica and other substances), viral or bacterial infections, and autoimmunity (the body's immune system attacking its own tissues and organs).
source_quote: Possible causes include: exposure to substances in the environment – such as mould, wood stoves, soil, tree pollen, insecticides, silica and other substances viral or bacterial infections the body’s immune system attacking its own tissues and organs (autoimmunity)

source_quote: Sarcoidosis can occasionally occur in more than one family member, but there's no evidence that the condition is inherited.

subject: Sarcoidosis
object: infectious, so it cannot be passed from person to person.
source_quote: The condition is not infectious, so it cannot be passed from person to person.

object: adults aged between 30 and 40; it can affect people of any age but is rare in childhood.
source_quote: Sarcoidosis can affect people of any age, but usually starts in adults aged between 30 and 40. It's rare in childhood.

object: women than men, and affects people from all ethnic backgrounds.
source_quote: The condition affects people from all ethnic backgrounds. It's also more common in women than men.

subject: Some people with sarcoidosis
object: no symptoms at all, and the condition is diagnosed after an X-ray carried out for another reason.
source_quote: Some people do not have any symptoms at all, and the condition is diagnosed after an X-ray carried out for another reason.

subject: The organs sarcoidosis most often affects
object: the lungs, skin and lymph nodes (glands).
source_quote: Sarcoidosis most often affects the lungs, skin and lymph nodes (glands).

subject: The lungs
object: about 9 out of 10 people with sarcoidosis; this is known as pulmonary sarcoidosis.
source_quote: The lungs are affected in about 9 out of 10 of people with sarcoidosis. This is known as pulmonary sarcoidosis.

subject: The main symptoms of pulmonary sarcoidosis
object: shortness of breath and a persistent dry cough; some people have pain and discomfort in their chest, but this is uncommon.
source_quote: This is known as pulmonary sarcoidosis. The main symptoms are shortness of breath and a persistent dry cough. Some people with pulmonary sarcoidosis experience pain and discomfort in their chest, but this is uncommon.

subject: Skin involvement, which occurs in many people with sarcoidosis,
object: tender bumps or patches on the skin (particularly the lower legs and arms) as well as bumps on the upper body; these can be reddish-brown or purple, depending on skin colour and the type of sarcoidosis.
source_quote: The skin is also affected in many people with sarcoidosis. This can cause tender bumps or patches to develop on the skin (particularly the lower legs and arms), as well as bumps on the upper body. These can be reddish-brown or purple, depending on your skin colour and the type of sarcoidosis you have.

subject: If other organs are affected, a person with sarcoidosis
object: tender and swollen glands in the face, neck, armpits or groin; tiredness and a general feeling of being unwell; painful joints; red or sore eyes; an abnormal heart rhythm (arrhythmia); a blocked or stuffy nose; pain in the bones; kidney stones; or headache.
source_quote: If other organs are affected, you may also have some of the following symptoms: tender and swollen glands in the face, neck, armpits or groin tiredness and a general feeling of being unwell painful joints red or sore eyes an abnormal heart rhythm (arrhythmia) a blocked or stuffy nose pain in the bones kidney stones headache

subject: Most people with sarcoidosis
object: symptoms suddenly, but these usually clear within a few months or years and the condition does not come back; this is known as acute sarcoidosis.
source_quote: Most people with sarcoidosis develop symptoms suddenly, but these usually clear within a few months or years and the condition does not come back. This is known as acute sarcoidosis.

subject: A few people with sarcoidosis
object: their symptoms develop gradually and get worse over time, to the point where they become severely affected; lots of granulomas may form in an organ and prevent it from working properly. This is known as chronic sarcoidosis.
source_quote: A few people find their symptoms develop gradually and get worse over time, to the point where they become severely affected. Lots of granulomas may form in an organ and prevent it from working properly. This is known as chronic sarcoidosis.

subject: Most people with sarcoidosis
object: their symptoms have disappeared within a few years of their diagnosis.
source_quote: Most people with the condition find their symptoms have disappeared within a few years of their diagnosis.

subject: For some people with sarcoidosis,
relation: the condition slowly gets worse over time
object: and they end up with organ damage; for example, their lungs may stop working properly, causing increasing breathlessness.
source_quote: However, for some people the condition slowly gets worse over time and they end up with organ damage. For example, their lungs may stop working properly, causing increasing breathlessness.

subject: A person whose symptoms suggest pulmonary sarcoidosis (sarcoidosis affecting the lungs)
object: a chest X-ray or a CT scan of the lungs to look for signs of the condition.
source_quote: If your symptoms suggest you have pulmonary sarcoidosis (sarcoidosis affecting the lungs), you may have a chest X-ray or a CT scan of your lungs to look for signs of the condition.

subject: In some cases of suspected pulmonary sarcoidosis,
object: the inside of the lungs using an endoscope (a long, thin, flexible tube with a light source and a camera at the end) passed down the throat; a small sample of lung tissue may also be removed during this test to be studied under a microscope, which is known as a biopsy.
source_quote: If your symptoms suggest you have pulmonary sarcoidosis (sarcoidosis affecting the lungs), you may have a chest X-ray or a CT scan of your lungs to look for signs of the condition. In some cases, doctors may want to examine the inside of your lungs using a long, thin, flexible tube with a light source and a camera at the end (an endoscope) that's passed down your throat. A small sample of lung tissue may also be removed during this test so it can be studied under a microscope. This is known as a biopsy.

subject: If doctors think sarcoidosis may be affecting other organs, such as the skin, heart or eyes,

object: will usually be carried out.
source_quote: If doctors think you may have sarcoidosis affecting other organs – such as the skin, heart or eyes – scans or examinations of these areas will usually be carried out.

subject: Sarcoidosis
object: no cure, but its symptoms can usually be managed with medicine.
source_quote: There is currently no cure but symptoms can usually be managed with medicine.

subject: Many people with sarcoidosis
object: treatment, as the condition often goes away on its own, usually within a few months or years.
source_quote: Many people with sarcoidosis do not need treatment as the condition often goes away on its own, usually within a few months or years.

subject: When sarcoidosis is going away on its own and does not need treatment,
relation: simple lifestyle changes and over-the-counter painkillers (such as paracetamol or ibuprofen)
object: are often all that is needed to control the pain of any flare-ups.
source_quote: Many people with sarcoidosis do not need treatment as the condition often goes away on its own, usually within a few months or years. In this case, simple lifestyle changes and over-the-counter painkillers (such as paracetamol or ibuprofen) are often all that's needed to control the pain of any flare-ups.

subject: In people with sarcoidosis who are not having treatment,
object: to check whether it is getting any better or worse without treatment; this can be done with regular X-rays, breathing tests and blood tests.
source_quote: Many people with sarcoidosis do not need treatment as the condition often goes away on its own, usually within a few months or years. Doctors will monitor your condition to check if it's getting any better or worse without treatment. This can be done with regular X-rays, breathing tests and blood tests.

subject: If treatment for sarcoidosis is recommended,
object: this helps relieve symptoms and prevent damage to affected organs by reducing inflammation and preventing scarring.
source_quote: If treatment is recommended, steroid tablets are usually used. This helps relieve symptoms and prevent damage to affected organs by reducing inflammation and preventing scarring.

subject: Steroid tablets used to treat sarcoidosis
object: side effects such as weight gain and mood swings if taken in high doses, and other side effects such as weakening of the bones (osteoporosis) if taken for a long time; they are therefore only used when necessary.
source_quote: If treatment is recommended, steroid tablets are usually used. However, steroid tablets can cause side effects such as weight gain and mood swings if taken in high doses. Other side effects, such as weakening of the bones (osteoporosis), can also develop if steroids are taken for a long time. Therefore, they're only used when necessary.

subject: A person given steroid tablets for sarcoidosis
object: a high dose for a short period of time, before switching to a low dose for the months or years that follow; their condition will be monitored during this time to see how well the treatment is working.
source_quote: If treatment is recommended, steroid tablets are usually used. You may initially be given a high dose of steroid medicine for a short period of time, before switching to a low dose for the months or years that follow. Your condition will be monitored during this time to see how well the treatment is working.

subject: In some cases of sarcoidosis treated with steroids,
object: can help reduce the risk of osteoporosis caused by long-term use of steroid medicine, but they should be taken only if advised by a doctor.
source_quote: If treatment is recommended, steroid tablets are usually used. In some cases, taking calcium or vitamin D supplements can help reduce the risk of osteoporosis caused by long-term use of steroid medicine. However, you should only take these if advised to by a doctor.

subject: Taking steroid medicine
relation: may increase the risk of complications, including kidney stones, in
object: some people with sarcoidosis.
source_quote: Some people with sarcoidosis may have an increased risk of developing complications, including kidney stones, while taking steroid medicine.

subject: In sarcoidosis, other medicines
object: if steroids are not enough or there are concerns about side effects; in these cases an immunosuppressant might be recommended, which may help to improve symptoms by reducing the activity of the immune system.
source_quote: Other medicines may sometimes be used if steroids are not enough or there are concerns about side effects. In these cases, a medicine called an immunosuppressant might be recommended. This may help to improve your symptoms by reducing the activity of your immune system.
